DeviceComponentStorage

@memory_only
struct DeviceComponentStorage[*ComponentTypes: ComponentType]

Owns one byte-addressed device column per configured component type.

Each initialized column has an independent valid row count. Its buffer length is a byte capacity, at least the row count times the component size. Capacity and valid row counts never shrink; smaller uploads overwrite only their range and retain previously valid suffix rows.

Aliases

component_manager

The component manager assigning IDs to ComponentTypes.

component_manager = ComponentManager[ComponentTypes]

Columns

The type of the per-component device column array.

Columns = Array[Optional[DeviceBuffer[DType.uint8]], len[TypeList[values]](ComponentTypes)]

Parameters

  • *ComponentTypes (ComponentType): The component types managed by this storage.

Implemented traits

AnyType, Copyable, Deinitable, Movable

Copies a range of the device column for T into host memory.

def copy_to_host[T: ComponentType](self, column_ptr: Pointer[T, MutUntrackedOrigin], *, offset: Int = Int(0), length: Int = Int(-1))

Parameters:

  • T (ComponentType): The component type of the column to copy.

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • column_ptr (Pointer[T, MutUntrackedOrigin]): The host pointer to copy the range into.
  • offset (Int): The starting row of the range to copy.
  • length (Int): The number of rows to copy. A negative value (the default) copies every row from offset through the end of the column.

Raises:

Error: If offset/length describe a range outside the selected column’s valid row bounds, or if the device copy fails.

ensure_column

Ensures the device column for T exists and covers length rows.

def ensure_column[T: ComponentType](mut self, length: Int)

Creates or grows the column as needed, but uploads no data into it. Marks at least length rows valid for kernel output; the caller must write newly exposed rows before downloading them. Existing valid rows and capacity are retained when length is smaller. Used for a kernel component that is write-only for the current call: the column must exist before the kernel writes through it, but nothing needs uploading first, since a write-only component’s prior value is never read by the kernel.

Parameters:

  • T (ComponentType): The component type of the column to ensure.

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • length (Int): The minimum number of rows the column must cover.

Raises:

Error: If length is negative or device allocation fails.

reserve_column

Reserves device capacity without publishing unwritten logical rows.

def reserve_column[T: ComponentType](mut self, length: Int)

Existing valid rows survive growth. A new column allocates at least the initial capacity or requested rows; subsequent growth doubles byte capacity unless the request is larger. Smaller requests retain both capacity and valid length. Use ensure_column instead when promising output rows that a kernel will write.

Parameters:

  • T (ComponentType): The component type whose capacity to reserve.

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • length (Int): The minimum row capacity, which must be nonnegative.

Raises:

Error: If length is negative or device allocation or copying fails.

copy_from_host

Copies host data for T into the device column, growing it if needed.

def copy_from_host[mut: Bool, origin: Origin[mut=mut], //, T: ComponentType](mut self, data: Span[T, origin], *, offset: Int = Int(0))

Parameters:

  • mut (Bool): Whether the source span is mutable.
  • origin (Origin[mut=mut]): The origin of the source span.
  • T (ComponentType): The component type of the column to copy into.

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • data (Span[T, origin]): The host data to upload.
  • offset (Int): The starting row at which to write the data. Must be in [0, valid rows]; uploads may overwrite or append, but cannot leave an uninitialized gap. Smaller uploads retain the valid suffix. Empty uploads do not initialize a column.

Raises:

Error: If offset is outside the valid rows or allocating or copying the device buffer fails.

DeviceResourceStorage

@memory_only
struct DeviceResourceStorage[resources: Resources[resources.ResourceTypes, _readonly=resources._readonly, _writeonly=resources._writeonly]]

Owns one byte-addressed device buffer per resource type required by a kernel.

Mirrors DeviceComponentStorage, but keyed by position in resources instead of by a ComponentManager-assigned id: each kernel invocation uploads exactly the (small, fixed) set of resources it declared as required, rather than mirroring the whole resource table to the device.

Aliases

Buffers

The type of the per-resource device buffer array.

Buffers = Array[Optional[DeviceBuffer[DType.uint8]], len[Resources[ResourceTypes, _readonly=_readonly, _writeonly=_writeonly]](resources)]

Parameters

  • resources (Resources[resources.ResourceTypes, _readonly=resources._readonly, _writeonly=resources._writeonly]): The resource types this storage may hold buffers for.

Implemented traits

AnyType, Copyable, Deinitable, Movable

Methods

Expand all   Collapse all

__init__

Creates a device resource storage with no buffers uploaded yet.

def __init__(out self, var device_context: DeviceContext)

  • self (Self)

Self

upload

Copies value into a freshly allocated device buffer.

def upload[T: ResourceType](mut self, ref value: T)

The host value must remain alive until the queued copy completes. This copies only the value’s bytes, not any allocations it points to.

Parameters:

  • T (ResourceType): The type of the resource to upload. Must be part of resources.

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • value (T): The host-side resource value to copy to the device.

Raises:

Error: If allocating or copying the device buffer fails.

download

Copies the device buffer for T back into value.

def download[T: ResourceType](self, mut value: T)

Mirrors [.upload], but in the opposite direction: after a kernel that may have mutated the resource has run, this pulls its bytes back from the device buffer into the host-side value.

Parameters:

  • T (ResourceType): The type of the resource to download. Must have been DeviceResourceStorage.uploaded already.

Args:

  • self (Self)
  • value (T): The host-side resource value to overwrite with the device buffer’s contents.

Raises:

Error: If the resource has not been uploaded.
